proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Cedar Rain-Room

## The pitch

The best all-around answer: a dry, shaded cedar room that frames the existing pond as the view.

This is concept **301 of 25** and curator rank **#1**. The working installed range is **$32,000–$52,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Replace the raised beds and wispy shrub between the pond and house-side fence.
- **Tree decision:** Remove only the wispy multi-stem shrub in the build zone; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 12 x 12 ft clear cedar pergola expression with visible rafters and a waterproof charcoal standing-seam shed roof above.
- **All-weather roof:** Opaque standing-seam metal, 2:12 visual pitch, lined underside, gutter to rain garden.
- **Underfoot:** 13 x 13 ft charcoal permeable-paver patio with a light-gray soldier-course edge.
- **Approach:** Curving large-format basalt stepping slabs along the house-side of the pond.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round low gas fire table centered between two deep lounge chairs; conditional on the selected manual allowing covered use.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Orange honeysuckle on independent side cables, sword fern, evergreen huckleberry, salal, Japanese forest grass.

Warm downlights in beams, two path lights, subtle pond uplight. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# Research basis — Cedar Rain-Room

- Mountlake Terrace lists accessory structures within its building-permit program: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/177/Building-Permits>
- The current accessory-structure code includes a five-foot rear-setback pathway for detached structures under 250 square feet and under 12 feet high; verify the current parcel-specific interpretation before design: <https://ecode360.com/48224185>
- The city filing checklist asks for existing/proposed hard surface, setbacks, lot coverage, and roof/footing drain disposal: <https://cityofmlt.com/DocumentCenter/View/38341/Accessory-Structure>
- Mountlake Terrace stormwater/LID guidance should shape roof drainage and new patio area: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/1869/Stormwater-and-Low-Impact-Development-LI>
- Corrugated and multiwall polycarbonate need product-specific minimum slope and flashing details: <https://www.palram.com/blog/construction-architecture/designing-a-pitched-roof-extension/>
- Wisteria becomes heavy and needs very strong support plus twice-yearly pruning: <https://extension.oregonstate.edu/news/prune-wisteria-keep-its-spring-show-bounds>
- Orange honeysuckle is a PNW native vine suited to sun/part shade and hummingbird habitat: <https://wpcdn.web.wsu.edu/wp-ecommerce/uploads/sites/2/woocommerce_uploads/MISC0273-new-Logo24-jmv4rn.pdf>
- Outdoor gas fire-appliance clearances are product-specific. Some listed manuals allow covered installations at defined clearances while others prohibit overhead enclosure, so the selected manual controls: <https://manuals.plus/napoleon/sttr1-gpfr-tropez-patio-flame-fire-table-manual>
- Mountlake Terrace significant-tree rules and current tree initiatives should be checked before removing the build-zone tree/shrub: <https://ecode360.com/48224918>

Concept-specific proposition: **Opaque standing-seam metal, 2:12 visual pitch, lined underside, gutter to rain garden.** 42 in round low gas fire table centered between two deep lounge chairs; conditional on the selected manual allowing covered use.

# Rain-Chain Garden Pavilion

## The pitch

Makes Seattle rain part of the experience while protecting the pond from extra runoff.

This is concept **311 of 25** and curator rank **#2**. The working installed range is **$36,000–$59,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Garden-bed zone, with roof water directed away from pond into a planted basin.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 12 x 14 ft clear cedar roofed pergola with refined exposed beams.
- **All-weather roof:** Charcoal standing-seam shed roof, lined soffit, full gutter and sculptural rain chain.
- **Underfoot:** Permeable basalt-tone pavers pitched away from pond.
- **Approach:** Broad stepping-stone walk plus a three-foot pond maintenance spur.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round black stone fire table with two deep camel lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Rain-garden sedge, slough sedge, sword fern, huckleberry; orange honeysuckle on outer posts.

Integrated beam downlights, rain-chain uplight, pond-edge glow. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Daylight Cedar Canopy

## The pitch

Keeps the pergola look, admits soft daylight, and still works in rain.

This is concept **305 of 25** and curator rank **#3**. The working installed range is **$27,000–$44,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Garden-bed zone with the roof falling toward a planted rain strip.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 12 x 12 ft cedar pergola frame with closely spaced exposed rafters.
- **All-weather roof:** Bronze solar-control multiwall polycarbonate above rafters at a rain-shedding pitch, with gutter.
- **Underfoot:** Warm-gray permeable pavers.
- **Approach:** Irregular gray flagstone threaded through bark and ferns.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round stone-look gas fire table, two rust-colored lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Orange honeysuckle on outer post cables, evergreen huckleberry, sword fern, forest grass.

Warm rafter lights that glow through the translucent roof. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Black Louver Room

## The pitch

A compact modern outdoor room with the cleanest all-weather controls.

This is concept **304 of 25** and curator rank **#5**. The working installed range is **$45,000–$75,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Garden-bed zone, crisp rectangle parallel to fence.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 12 x 13 ft slim black aluminum pergola with integrated gutters and motorized closing louvers.
- **All-weather roof:** Motorized aluminum louvers that close for rain; hidden perimeter drainage.
- **Underfoot:** Large-format charcoal porcelain pavers with narrow joints.
- **Approach:** Straight stepping-slab walk aligned to one pavilion bay.
- **Seating/fire:** 36 in round black gas fire table and two low cream lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

No vines on moving roof; soft fern, carex, huckleberry and white hydrangea perimeter.

Integrated dimmable linear LEDs plus two pond-edge lights. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# Research basis — Black Louver Room

- Mountlake Terrace lists accessory structures within its building-permit program: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/177/Building-Permits>
- The current accessory-structure code includes a five-foot rear-setback pathway for detached structures under 250 square feet and under 12 feet high; verify the current parcel-specific interpretation before design: <https://ecode360.com/48224185>
- The city filing checklist asks for existing/proposed hard surface, setbacks, lot coverage, and roof/footing drain disposal: <https://cityofmlt.com/DocumentCenter/View/38341/Accessory-Structure>
- Mountlake Terrace stormwater/LID guidance should shape roof drainage and new patio area: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/1869/Stormwater-and-Low-Impact-Development-LI>
- Corrugated and multiwall polycarbonate need product-specific minimum slope and flashing details: <https://www.palram.com/blog/construction-architecture/designing-a-pitched-roof-extension/>
- Wisteria becomes heavy and needs very strong support plus twice-yearly pruning: <https://extension.oregonstate.edu/news/prune-wisteria-keep-its-spring-show-bounds>
- Orange honeysuckle is a PNW native vine suited to sun/part shade and hummingbird habitat: <https://wpcdn.web.wsu.edu/wp-ecommerce/uploads/sites/2/woocommerce_uploads/MISC0273-new-Logo24-jmv4rn.pdf>
- Outdoor gas fire-appliance clearances are product-specific. Some listed manuals allow covered installations at defined clearances while others prohibit overhead enclosure, so the selected manual controls: <https://manuals.plus/napoleon/sttr1-gpfr-tropez-patio-flame-fire-table-manual>
- Mountlake Terrace significant-tree rules and current tree initiatives should be checked before removing the build-zone tree/shrub: <https://ecode360.com/48224918>

Concept-specific proposition: **Motorized aluminum louvers that close for rain; hidden perimeter drainage.** 36 in round black gas fire table and two low cream lounge chairs.

# Wisteria Gable Gallery

## The pitch

A romantic garden folly with disciplined vine support and true Seattle rain protection.

This is concept **302 of 25** and curator rank **#6**. The working installed range is **$42,000–$68,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Garden-bed zone, long side parallel to the rear fence.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 12 x 14 ft heavy cedar pavilion with an airy gable and expressed timber truss.
- **All-weather roof:** Waterproof charcoal standing-seam gable roof with gutters on both eaves.
- **Underfoot:** Thermal bluestone patio over a drained compacted base.
- **Approach:** Three-foot bluestone walk tangent to the pond, never crossing its rim.
- **Seating/fire:** 36 in round gas fire table under the ridge between two camel sling lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

One wisteria trained on an independent exterior cable frame kept off roof and gutters; ferns and hydrangea below.

Tiny truss uplights, warm pendants, pond-edge pin lights. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

# Covered Chairs, Open-Sky Fire

## The pitch

The safest flexible fire strategy if the preferred table manual forbids overhead cover.

This is concept **318 of 25** and curator rank **#7**. The working installed range is **$26,000–$45,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Lawn edge near pond, with the fire table just beyond the roof dripline.
- **Tree decision:** Retain mature trees; remove only clutter and simplify raised beds.
- **Structure:** 10 x 12 ft cedar rain pergola covering two lounge chairs and a small side table.
- **All-weather roof:** Bronze multiwall polycarbonate above exposed rafters.
- **Underfoot:** 14 x 16 ft permeable-paver patio extending beyond roof.
- **Approach:** Short paver connector from pond path.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round gas fire table placed in the open patio beyond roof; chairs can pivot toward it.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Orange honeysuckle on rear cable, ferns and huckleberry.

Roof downlights, open-patio bollard, pond sparkle lights. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Northwest Hip-Roof Gazebo

## The pitch

The most classically sheltered option, softened into a Pacific Northwest garden pavilion.

This is concept **303 of 25** and curator rank **#8**. The working installed range is **$38,000–$62,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Garden-bed zone, centered behind and to the right of the pond.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 12 ft square open-sided cedar gazebo with substantial posts and a shallow hip roof.
- **All-weather roof:** Charcoal architectural shingles with concealed gutters and a cedar tongue-and-groove ceiling.
- **Underfoot:** 13 ft square exposed-aggregate concrete with basalt border.
- **Approach:** Short fan of basalt stepping stones from lawn to pavilion.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round concrete-look gas fire table with two moss-green swivel lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Layered sword ferns, compact rhododendron, huckleberry, mossy basalt boulders.

Ceiling downlights and low boulder grazing lights. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# Pond Courtyard Connector

## The pitch

The most coherent whole-yard circulation plan and easiest everyday access.

This is concept **321 of 25** and curator rank **#10**. The working installed range is **$42,000–$69,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Garden-bed zone with a generous hardscape connector between house, pavilion, and pond.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the wispy shrub and raised beds; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 11 x 13 ft cedar roofed pergola at the far end of a compact courtyard.
- **All-weather roof:** Lined standing-seam shed roof.
- **Underfoot:** Permeable paver courtyard with planted joints at the outer edges.
- **Approach:** Continuous accessible paver route with a three-foot maintenance bypass.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round gas fire table with two swivel lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Ferns and grasses in slot beds, huckleberry screen, no roof vines.

Courtyard step lights, warm roof lights, subtle underwater pond lighting. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Cantilever Pond Frame

## The pitch

Maximizes the unobstructed view of the pond with the least visible front structure.

This is concept **308 of 25** and curator rank **#12**. The working installed range is **$48,000–$76,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Garden-bed zone with two rear posts and a visually open pond-facing edge.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 10 x 14 ft engineered black-steel rear frame with warm cedar ceiling and open cantilevered front edge.
- **All-weather roof:** Insulated low-slope metal roof draining to rear gutter.
- **Underfoot:** Rectilinear charcoal pavers floating in dark gravel.
- **Approach:** Straight paver ribbon from lawn, visually continuing under roof.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round concrete fire table and two walnut-toned sling chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Low sedges, sword fern, salal; no roof vines.

Linear ceiling wash, post lights, water shimmer light. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

- The city filing checklist asks for existing/proposed hard surface, setbacks, lot coverage, and roof/footing drain disposal: <https://cityofmlt.com/DocumentCenter/View/38341/Accessory-Structure>
- Mountlake Terrace stormwater/LID guidance should shape roof drainage and new patio area: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/1869/Stormwater-and-Low-Impact-Development-LI>
- Corrugated and multiwall polycarbonate need product-specific minimum slope and flashing details: <https://www.palram.com/blog/construction-architecture/designing-a-pitched-roof-extension/>
- Wisteria becomes heavy and needs very strong support plus twice-yearly pruning: <https://extension.oregonstate.edu/news/prune-wisteria-keep-its-spring-show-bounds>
- Orange honeysuckle is a PNW native vine suited to sun/part shade and hummingbird habitat: <https://wpcdn.web.wsu.edu/wp-ecommerce/uploads/sites/2/woocommerce_uploads/MISC0273-new-Logo24-jmv4rn.pdf>
- Outdoor gas fire-appliance clearances are product-specific. Some listed manuals allow covered installations at defined clearances while others prohibit overhead enclosure, so the selected manual controls: <https://manuals.plus/napoleon/sttr1-gpfr-tropez-patio-flame-fire-table-manual>
- Mountlake Terrace significant-tree rules and current tree initiatives should be checked before removing the build-zone tree/shrub: <https://ecode360.com/48224918>

proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Pond-Axis Pavilion

## The pitch

A bold architectural frame that makes the pond the center of every seated view.

This is concept **315 of 25** and curator rank **#14**. The working installed range is **$42,000–$68,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Lawn-side, centered on the pond's viewing axis but outside its stone rim.
- **Tree decision:** Retain mature trees; simplify raised beds into bark and ferns.
- **Structure:** 11 x 14 ft black steel and cedar pavilion with open pond-facing bay.
- **All-weather roof:** Low opaque standing-seam shed roof.
- **Underfoot:** Long rectangular bluestone terrace.
- **Approach:** Direct bluestone walk framing the pond rather than touching it.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round gas fire table with two cognac chairs facing pond.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Structured sedges, ferns, huckleberry, no vines.

Minimal linear roof light and pond grazing lights. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# Compact Rain Pergola

## The pitch

The most attainable version that is still genuinely dry and comfortable.

This is concept **310 of 25** and curator rank **#17**. The working installed range is **$14,000–$26,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Smallest viable footprint in the garden-bed zone.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 10 x 12 ft pressure-treated frame faced with cedar trim and visible pergola rafters.
- **All-weather roof:** Opal corrugated polycarbonate at manufacturer-compliant pitch with an exposed gutter.
- **Underfoot:** Compacted crushed-granite patio with a paver fire-table pad.
- **Approach:** Simple gravel route edged in steel.
- **Seating/fire:** 36 in round gas fire table and two compact sling lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Orange honeysuckle on one side panel, durable ferns and salal.

Plug-in-rated warm café strand under roof plus two solar-quality path lights. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# House-Side Rain Terrace

## The pitch

The driest route from indoors, but attachment and drainage make it more technically involved.

This is concept **319 of 25** and curator rank **#19**. The working installed range is **$40,000–$70,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Attached or near-attached to the house-side edge, looking across the pond.
- **Tree decision:** Remove the wispy shrub against the house-side build area; arborist review if trunk qualifies.
- **Structure:** 12 x 14 ft cedar lean-to patio cover with open sides.
- **All-weather roof:** Standing-seam metal roof tied into a properly flashed wall ledger or independently posted near the wall.
- **Underfoot:** Expanded paver terrace continuous with house access.
- **Approach:** Paver apron narrowing to flagstone along pond.
- **Seating/fire:** 42 in round gas fire table with two deep chairs; product-specific covered-use approval required.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Ferns, forest grass, huckleberry; no vines at wall or gutter.

Ceiling downlights and wall sconces. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Lawn Jewel Gazebo

## The pitch

A romantic object in the lawn, dramatic but it consumes the most open grass.

This is concept **313 of 25** and curator rank **#21**. The working installed range is **$36,000–$58,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** On a new circular patio in the open lawn left of the pond.
- **Tree decision:** Retain the build-zone shrub and all mature trees; raised beds become planted border.
- **Structure:** 12 ft octagonal cedar gazebo with open rails only on two rear facets.
- **All-weather roof:** Charcoal shingle octagonal roof with vented cap.
- **Underfoot:** 14 ft circular permeable-paver terrace.
- **Approach:** Curving three-foot paver walk from pond and house.
- **Seating/fire:** 36 in round gas fire table with two curved lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Low meadow ring, compact huckleberry, grasses, no roof vines.

Ceiling pendant, path lights, soft meadow uplights. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# Research basis — Lawn Jewel Gazebo

- Mountlake Terrace lists accessory structures within its building-permit program: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/177/Building-Permits>
- The current accessory-structure code includes a five-foot rear-setback pathway for detached structures under 250 square feet and under 12 feet high; verify the current parcel-specific interpretation before design: <https://ecode360.com/48224185>
- The city filing checklist asks for existing/proposed hard surface, setbacks, lot coverage, and roof/footing drain disposal: <https://cityofmlt.com/DocumentCenter/View/38341/Accessory-Structure>
- Mountlake Terrace stormwater/LID guidance should shape roof drainage and new patio area: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/1869/Stormwater-and-Low-Impact-Development-LI>
- Corrugated and multiwall polycarbonate need product-specific minimum slope and flashing details: <https://www.palram.com/blog/construction-architecture/designing-a-pitched-roof-extension/>
- Wisteria becomes heavy and needs very strong support plus twice-yearly pruning: <https://extension.oregonstate.edu/news/prune-wisteria-keep-its-spring-show-bounds>
- Orange honeysuckle is a PNW native vine suited to sun/part shade and hummingbird habitat: <https://wpcdn.web.wsu.edu/wp-ecommerce/uploads/sites/2/woocommerce_uploads/MISC0273-new-Logo24-jmv4rn.pdf>
- Outdoor gas fire-appliance clearances are product-specific. Some listed manuals allow covered installations at defined clearances while others prohibit overhead enclosure, so the selected manual controls: <https://manuals.plus/napoleon/sttr1-gpfr-tropez-patio-flame-fire-table-manual>
- Mountlake Terrace significant-tree rules and current tree initiatives should be checked before removing the build-zone tree/shrub: <https://ecode360.com/48224918>

Concept-specific proposition: **Charcoal shingle octagonal roof with vented cap.** 36 in round gas fire table with two curved lounge chairs.

proposals.reportMarkdown:
# Meadow Walk Pavilion

## The pitch

Creates a journey and seasonal habitat, trading lawn simplicity for atmosphere.

This is concept **317 of 25** and curator rank **#23**. The working installed range is **$28,000–$48,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Farther into the lawn, reached through a curved low meadow.
- **Tree decision:** Retain build-zone shrub and mature trees.
- **Structure:** 10 x 12 ft simple cedar pavilion.
- **All-weather roof:** Opaque green standing-seam gable roof.
- **Underfoot:** Compact flagstone rectangle.
- **Approach:** Curved mower-width gravel path through a low PNW meadow.
- **Seating/fire:** 36 in round gas fire table with two cedar lounge chairs.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Tufted hairgrass, yarrow, camas, selfheal, compact shrubs at edges.

Very low shielded path markers and pavilion pendant. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# Pond-Edge Boardwalk Room

## The pitch

The closest pond experience, with higher waterproofing and maintenance complexity.

This is concept **323 of 25** and curator rank **#24**. The working installed range is **$39,000–$65,000** before survey surprises, utility work, permitting, engineering, or major tree work.

## Site move

- **Placement:** Beside—not over—the pond, with a short raised boardwalk landing outside the stone rim.
- **Tree decision:** Remove build-zone shrub; retain mature trees.
- **Structure:** 10 x 13 ft cedar rain pergola offset from pond by a full maintenance strip.
- **All-weather roof:** Bronze multiwall polycarbonate above cedar rafters.
- **Underfoot:** Low thermally modified wood deck over pin footings, separated from pond stones.
- **Approach:** Short non-slip boardwalk with gravel maintenance bypass.
- **Seating/fire:** 36 in round gas fire table on a noncombustible inset; covered-use listing required.

The existing pond is fixed. The proposal keeps a **minimum three-foot service path** outside its stone rim, finishes exposed weed barrier with bark, and uses the pond as the primary seated view.

## Planting and atmosphere

Ferns, sedges, huckleberry, no vine over water.

Recessed low deck lights and pond reflections. Roof runoff should be collected and directed away from the pond to a tested dispersal or planted rain-garden area.

## Why it could win

- It provides true rain cover, not decorative slats alone.
- Two comfortable chairs and the round fire table remain the only primary furniture, so the room does not feel crowded.
- Bark, path, edge planting, and lighting make the pond landscape feel complete.
- The design is scaled around a 12-foot-class room rather than an oversized entertainment pavilion.

## Watch-outs

- Dimensions shown are planning estimates from photographs, not a survey.
- Verify property lines, easements, utilities, setbacks, height, lot coverage, drainage, footings, and permit scope with Mountlake Terrace.
- Select the gas fire table before finalizing the roof. The exact ANSI-listed product manual must expressly allow covered use at the designed overhead and side clearances; otherwise use the adjacent open-sky variation.
- Tree removal or work in a significant-tree root zone may trigger arborist and city review.
- Vines belong on an independent side cable/trellis, kept off the hot roof membrane, gutters, and fire plume.

## Image-reading note

The current photographs are the site record. ImageGen mockups are comparative design studies and may redraw small natural details; they are not construction documents and never authorize a change to the pond.

# Research basis — Pond-Edge Boardwalk Room

- Mountlake Terrace lists accessory structures within its building-permit program: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/177/Building-Permits>
- The current accessory-structure code includes a five-foot rear-setback pathway for detached structures under 250 square feet and under 12 feet high; verify the current parcel-specific interpretation before design: <https://ecode360.com/48224185>
- The city filing checklist asks for existing/proposed hard surface, setbacks, lot coverage, and roof/footing drain disposal: <https://cityofmlt.com/DocumentCenter/View/38341/Accessory-Structure>
- Mountlake Terrace stormwater/LID guidance should shape roof drainage and new patio area: <https://www.cityofmlt.com/1869/Stormwater-and-Low-Impact-Development-LI>
- Corrugated and multiwall polycarbonate need product-specific minimum slope and flashing details: <https://www.palram.com/blog/construction-architecture/designing-a-pitched-roof-extension/>
- Wisteria becomes heavy and needs very strong support plus twice-yearly pruning: <https://extension.oregonstate.edu/news/prune-wisteria-keep-its-spring-show-bounds>
- Orange honeysuckle is a PNW native vine suited to sun/part shade and hummingbird habitat: <https://wpcdn.web.wsu.edu/wp-ecommerce/uploads/sites/2/woocommerce_uploads/MISC0273-new-Logo24-jmv4rn.pdf>
- Outdoor gas fire-appliance clearances are product-specific. Some listed manuals allow covered installations at defined clearances while others prohibit overhead enclosure, so the selected manual controls: <https://manuals.plus/napoleon/sttr1-gpfr-tropez-patio-flame-fire-table-manual>
- Mountlake Terrace significant-tree rules and current tree initiatives should be checked before removing the build-zone tree/shrub: <https://ecode360.com/48224918>

Concept-specific proposition: **Bronze multiwall polycarbonate above cedar rafters.** 36 in round gas fire table on a noncombustible inset; covered-use listing required.

LOCKED SITE INVARIANTS: The completed pond is existing and expensive. Keep its precise position, irregular outline, water, waterfall, every visible gray ledgestone, aquatic plants, lily pads, and relationship to fence and lawn recognizably identical. Preserve camera angle, horizon, lens, property fences, lattice, house/outbuilding edges, mature conifers, neighbor roofs and neighbor yard beyond the fence. Never invent property outside the fence. Do not bridge, deck over, shrink, enlarge, relocate, simplify, replace, or redesign the pond.

PROPOSAL: Far-Corner Tea House. Creates the strongest sense of escape but the longest utility run and least convenient rainy access.
PLACEMENT: Place the structure in the far user-lawn corner, not beyond the perimeter fence, reached by a curved path from the pond. Far lawn corner beyond the pond, creating a destination view back toward water.
TREE DECISION: Retain build-zone shrub and mature trees; remove only low conflicting plants at pavilion.
STRUCTURE: 10 x 12 ft dark cedar pavilion with a low gable.
WATERPROOF ROOF: Charcoal standing-seam gable roof.
FLOOR: Compact basalt-paver terrace.
PATH: Long curved flagstone garden walk skirting pond.
FURNISHING: Exactly two comfortable adult lounge chairs and 36 in round gas fire table with two teak lounge chairs.
PLANTING: Layered huckleberry, vine maple, ferns, woodland groundcovers.
LIGHTING: Lantern-like pendant, long low path lights.

FINISH THE WHOLE SCENE: Remove temporary chairs, tools, buckets, cords, loose stone piles, folded loose fabric and construction clutter. Cover every exposed black weed-barrier area with a clean three-inch layer of natural medium-dark fir/hemlock bark mulch, precisely fitted around the unchanged pond stones and plants. Repair disturbed lawn realistically. Keep a clear three-foot pond maintenance route. Add controlled PNW planting pockets, a coherent path/patio connection, physically plausible roof gutters/downspout or rain chain draining away from the pond, and enticing warm early-evening light. The pavilion must be open on at least two sides and believable in scale for two chairs plus the round fire table.

AESTHETIC: Better Homes & Gardens editorial photorealism at this exact modest Seattle-area suburban property—aspirational, warm, lush, buildable, and believable, not a fantasy estate. Keep the pond prominent as the hero foreground element. No people, text, labels, logos, arrows, split screen, borders, extra ponds, swimming pool, outdoor kitchen, sofa set, dining set, or more than two lounge chairs. One raster image only.
acceptanceCriteria: existing pond remains recognizably fixed
camera and property boundary match source
proposal placement matches concept
exactly two lounge chairs and one round fire table
bark covers exposed weed barrier
path, planting, rain handling, and warm lighting complete the scene
no text, no extra pond, no invented neighbor-yard construction
